title: Penetrating damp vs roof defect — top-floor ceiling by the chimney breast, no roof access
why: Staining to a top-floor ceiling beside a chimney breast. Candidates: flashing/roof covering, a defective chimney stack/pot, a gutter over-spilling onto the wall, or a historic leak. No roof access, no readings at height. The finding must not assert a roof defect it never saw.

room.name: Bedroom 2
room.note: Brown staining to ceiling against the chimney breast, extends about a metre along the junction. Plaster sounds hollow when tapped. Couldn't get onto the roof; from the garden the gutter on that side looked full of moss.

transcripts: Back bedroom, staining to the ceiling right up against the chimney breast, runs along that junction maybe a metre. Tapped it, sounds hollow, plaster's probably blown. Can't get on the roof, no ladder tall enough. From the garden the gutter that side is full of moss and there's a plant growing out of it. Could be the flashing round the stack, could be the gutter, can't say from here.

must_not_happen.label: no roof element stated defective when none was inspected
no high confidence in an uninspected cause
no duty-of-care citation without a risk-to-person basis

allowed_uncertainty: Roof/flashing, chimney, or gutter as candidates; preferred cause may be 'water ingress from the roof or rainwater goods' with investigation_first.
reviewer_notes: Surveyor's own words: 'can't say from here'. That must survive.
